sections.title: What you know
sections.content: In B2 Unit 13 you used *que* + subjunctive for a person or thing you cannot point at. Now the speaker does not care which one it is. *Cualquiera que* means "whichever" or "anyone who", *quienquiera que* means "whoever" and *dondequiera que* means "wherever". All three take the subjunctive, because the answer is left open: it could be anyone, anywhere. You know the shorter *pase lo que pase* from B2 Unit 8, with *venga quien venga* and *estés donde estés* beside it; these forms say the same kind of thing in a different shape.

sections.title: Three new words
rows: Cualquiera que llegue temprano puede entrar.
Anyone who arrives early can come in.
Quienquiera que llame, dile que no estoy.
Whoever calls, tell them I'm not in.
Dondequiera que vayas, te voy a llamar.
Wherever you go, I'm going to call you.
Cualquiera que sea la respuesta, la acepto.
Whatever the answer is, I accept it.

sections.title: How to use them
sections.content: *Cualquiera* is a pronoun: it stands alone or comes before *que*. Before a noun it becomes *cualquier*: *cualquier persona que llegue*. *Quienquiera* and *dondequiera* are each one word. After all of them comes *que* and the subjunctive. *Cualquiera que sea…* is the usual way to say "whatever … is".

items.spanish: Cualquier persona que llegue tarde tiene que esperar.
items.english: Anyone who arrives late has to wait.

items.spanish: Quienquiera que haya llamado, no dejó ningún recado.
Dondequiera que estés, piensa en nosotros.
items.english: Wherever you are, think of us.

sections.content: The subjunctive says "it does not matter which". When you talk about a real, known person, use an ordinary relative with the indicative: *La persona que llamó dejó un recado*. Never write *cualquier que*: *cualquiera* loses its final *-a* only before a noun.
